cells.act: work the pattern through to its logic
cells.ask: Take a possibility you're holding open and follow it on paper to where it lands. Walk the line start to end, then mark it possible or dead.
cells.core:
You're holding a wide set of possibilities open right now, and you're doing it honestly. Nothing is forced into a conclusion before its time. You can name what each option would actually feel like, and you can see the shape underneath them — which ones are really the same choice wearing different clothes. That kind of seeing is a skill, not a stall, and it's what makes the gather trustworthy rather than just restless.

The next good thing this can be is a deliberate check. Take a possibility you're holding open, and follow it on paper to where it lands. Walk the line start to end, then mark it possible or dead. If it holds, you'll know it for a reason instead of a mood; if it falls apart, you've cleared the table a little without losing anything. You have that skill and you can use it on purpose rather than by reflex.

cells.tense: The next move is being planned for a feeling that hasn't shown up yet, and it can't be planned for.
cells.act: keep what the change produced from drifting
cells.ask: Choose a possibility you've already thought through and put down its smallest first step. One line — nothing follows it.
cells.core:
You can feel the possible versions of this before they arrive, and there are more of them than anyone could act on. So the planning gets there first — scenarios built out for feelings that haven't come, and the ones that do come get measured against a script instead of just being felt. The gathering has gotten loud enough that it's standing in for the thing itself.

What settles it is giving one piece a fixed shape. Choose a possibility you've already thought through and put down its smallest first step. One line, no timeline, nothing follows it. The rest don't need closing. What was gathered and worked through gets a form, and the form is what holds while feeling swings.

cells.tense: The possibilities were gathered once, and the door to acting on any of them is already shut.
cells.act: let the mind rest instead of working the problem
cells.ask: Leave the whole list alone this afternoon. Go do something with your hands that needs no deciding, and see how long you can leave it be.
cells.core:
The possibilities were laid out once, and you haven't moved past the laying out. From where you stand now it reads as too late to choose any of them, so none got chosen, and what's left is a catalog of maybes you keep checking. The range is still there, and it's costing you something to keep holding it.

More sorting won't do it. It's a rest. Leave the whole list alone this afternoon and go do something with your hands that needs no deciding. When the mind comes back, it comes back calibrated — the options look their real size, and the one worth doing tends to be plain without you forcing it. You don't have to close anything to stop carrying it around.

cells.tense: The line through all these possibilities is already being drawn, and the hand drawing it isn't noticed.
cells.act: reason it from first principles once
cells.ask: Reason one possibility from first principles once — what it actually needs, from nothing. Notice which rule you used, and leave it at that.
cells.core:
There's already a rule running under all of this — something that decides which possibilities count and which get set aside. It's yours, and it works. Asked, you'd say the options are just obviously uneven, that some are plainly stronger. The weighing is happening somewhere, and it mostly isn't showing up as a decision.

Reason one possibility from first principles once — what it actually needs, starting from nothing. The rule you reach for shows itself in the working. Notice which one it was, and leave it there. If it holds, you keep it with your eyes open, which is different from keeping it by habit. If it doesn't, you've found the invisible part, and you can change one rule instead of wrestling forty options.
